scope: Read-only source and existing vmlinux audit of BE19000AI kernel8; no source/build changes, no SSH, and no live syscall execution in this audit.

verdict.native_aarch64: Ordinary native clock/timer/futex/etc. interfaces already use 64-bit seconds. They do not need or use the AArch32 403-423 numbers. This is not a claim that every file format, driver ioctl or socket option has complete Y2038 coverage.
verdict.aarch32_compat: None of the 20 assigned time64 syscall numbers in 403-423 are wired. The table has 399 entries, numbered 0-398. Number 415 is reserved, not an omitted implementation.
verdict.configuration: CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME=y preserves the OLD 32-bit time_t compat ABI; it does not enable the new time64 syscalls. CONFIG_64BIT_TIME and CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_64BIT_TIME are not enabled in this configuration.
verdict.provenance: The inspected syscall tables, dispatch, time helpers and principal clock implementation are byte-identical to the checked-out source base; none of the six recorded local patches adds the missing time64 syscall series.

statx.limits: A time64-capable statx ABI does not extend a filesystem's actual timestamp range or force every requested field to be supported. Userspace must use a suitable API and check stx_mask.

legacy_stat.status: native generic stat uses 64-bit long seconds; compat stat/stat64 remain 32-bit time fields
legacy_stat.limits: The stat64 name widens file size/inode-related fields; it does not imply 64-bit timestamps. The compat stat64 fields are u32 compat_ulong_t, while other compat stat fields use signed compat_time_t. Neither is a 64-bit seconds ABI.

socket_timestamps.status: SO_TIMESTAMP_NEW, SO_TIMESTAMPNS_NEW and SO_TIMESTAMPING_NEW are absent from UAPI and SOL_SOCKET handling; only the older timestamp options are supported here. New timeout options are also absent.

socket_timestamps.assessment: Native AArch64 old timestamp options carry native long/64-bit time fields. AArch32 ancillary data is explicitly converted to 32-bit compat timeval/timespec. Thus current native functionality is not equivalent to support for all modern *_NEW options. Rebuilding 32-bit userspace with 64-bit time_t alone cannot supply missing kernel ABI.

backport_scope_caution: Do not fix this by only increasing the syscall count or pointing every new number at an existing compat handler. Existing compat handlers consume time32. Native handlers for fd sets, signal sets, mmsghdr and timex may also have different non-time ABI layouts; a coherent upstream time64 series and ABI-specific marshalling are required. Existing internal timespec64 helpers do not imply exported AArch32 time64 support.
runtime_scope: Raw live probes are handled separately by the parent. This report predicts ENOSYS for absent AArch32 numbers from source and ELF; it does not claim to have executed them or to have tested timestamps beyond 2038.

provenance.historical_limit: The source checkout is shallow. Equality to this vendor/Merlin source base and absence from the six local patches are verified; the original upstream introduction history of every existing preparatory helper is not reconstructed here.
